items.title: Tomorrow Is Another Chance
items.moral: Moral: Every day is a new page. You can't change yesterday, but how you write today is in your hands.
body: One day follows another. Some end happily; others bring disappointment. Whatever remains unfinished today, do not dwell on “I failed” or “I couldn’t do it.” Above all, do not lose hope. When the sun rises tomorrow, a whole new day will be yours.

items.title: How We Express Sorrow
items.moral: Moral: People carry their problems in different ways: some talk, some write, some keep quiet and smile. The deepest problems are often hidden in the deepest silence.
body: Someone who explains a problem plainly seeks a solution. Someone who describes it beautifully is a writer; someone who speaks of it with love is a lover. Someone who conceals it behind a smile is a sage.

items.title: Come Again Soon
items.moral: Moral: A subtle gesture can convey great kindness. The value given to a person is often seen in small moments.
body: In an Ottoman custom, a host placed a departing guest’s shoes at the door with their toes pointing into the house. Putting them on turned the guest back toward the home, as though returning. The gesture meant, “Go safely, and come again.”

items.title: Land and Homeland
items.moral: Moral: Sacrifice gives a homeland its profound meaning. It is more than a place; it is land held sacred by those who have suffered for it.
body: Mix earth with water and it becomes mud. Mix it with blood and it becomes a homeland.

items.title: Honey or Dry Bread?
items.moral: Moral: Your companions can lift you up or lead you astray. Plain bread shared with a wise person is worth more than honey shared with a fool.
body: It is better to sit with a scholar and eat dry bread than to sit with an ignorant man and eat honey.

items.title: Wasted Effort
items.moral: Moral: Choosing your company helps shape your life. Do not waste it arguing with people unwilling to learn or trusting those who are insincere.
body: It is futile to advise a fool, to argue with an ignorant person, to befriend a hypocrite.

items.title: Know Your Friend
items.moral: Moral: A friend is known in trouble, in hardship, and in the test of advantage. Everyone is a friend in good times; a true friend is revealed in adversity.
body: To know a friend’s character, watch how they face trouble, hardship, and disagreement. Then see how they act when their own interests are at stake.

items.moral: Moral: Give your time to relationships that bring love and joy into your life.
body: Life is short. Spend it with people who bring you happiness and make you feel loved.

items.title: Living in the Past
items.moral: Moral: You cannot undo the past. Turn toward the future and give yourself a chance to move forward.
body: Living in the past is like walking backward. With your eyes turned away from the road ahead, you stumble—unable either to change what lies behind you or to reach what lies before you.

items.title: A Mature Person
items.moral: Moral: Maturity is the ability to step away from harmful relationships and protect one’s inner peace. Knowing whom—and what—to keep at a distance is also a form of wisdom.
body: There comes a time when you value old friends’ sincerity more than passing acquaintances. You step away from ignorance and relationships that disturb your peace. That is one sign of growing maturity.

items.title: May You Always Have Reason to Smile
items.moral: Moral: Warmth draws people to us. A smile costs nothing, yet can make all the difference.
body: A person who sells vinegar with a smile will have more customers than a person who sells honey with a frown.

items.moral: Moral: Unwanted advice can become a burden. Calling interference “kindness” does not prevent it from doing harm.
body: May Allah never leave anyone so idle that they have time to meddle in other people’s lives!
